title: Accelerating Scientific Research in Health Data Science With Muse Models
key_facts: Meta built a human-led AI system for health research on a coding scaffold powered by Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder.
It could access public data and a licensed retrospective database of five million de-identified electronic health records.
Medical researchers (cardiology, epidemiology, infectious disease, internal medicine) used it over four weeks to brainstorm hypotheses, write code and draft manuscripts.
Meta published ten manuscripts, each checked by peers, a biostatistician and third-party independent experts.
Example: after infective endocarditis, patients had a 73% higher rate of new arrhythmias than patients with bacteremia alone (one-year risk 7% vs 4%).
An outside cardiologist called that study hypothesis generating rather than practice changing.
Meta says understanding of using AI for health research is still relatively early.
quote_evidence: In this initial exploration, we developed a human-led AI system for conducting health research, in which AI accelerates each stage of research while domain experts remain responsible for the scientific decisions and conclusions.
Today we are sharing ten research manuscripts generated throughout this process
I would consider this hypothesis generating rather than practice changing with regards to the conclusions.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how much of the work of a medical study an AI model can do, but results come from the company itself and from observational data.
notes: Company's own blog (39,000 characters read in part); expert reviews are quoted by Meta, not independent reporting. Muse models are Meta's own AI models.
